engagement_title: Anvil and Oak strength studio launch: recover the mark off the painted brick, bring three evenings of member-athlete portraits to one look, rebuild the athlete cards from the barbell club's press file, and hand back the schedule poster, the membership deck and the spotlight set as documents the coaches can edit themselves
vertical: Health and fitness, an independent strength and functional training studio opening in a converted machine shop in Providence, Rhode Island
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the recurring Upwork gym-launch posting in which an owner opening a new studio asks for 'a class schedule poster for the wall, a membership deck we use at the front desk, and social posts for Instagram, all in our branding', explicitly noting that they have 'no logo file, only a photo of the sign' and that the schedule 'changes every season so we need to be able to edit it ourselves'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com posting from a barbell and powerlifting club needing 'individual athlete result cards, one per lifter, print ready, from the template our old designer made', with only the printed PDF surviving and a spreadsheet of names and numbers supplied alongside. Both real clients, their gyms and their coaches are laundered to the fictional Anvil and Oak. The ledger's STRENGTHEN verdict was right that the concept as banked leaned on authoring alone: the fuller commission this client genuinely has starts at a photograph of a hand-painted mark and sixteen inconsistent portraits, runs through a real record-per-page card run inherited from a printer who is gone, and only then reaches the poster, the deck and the spotlight set that all have to carry the same recovered mark identically.
client_one_liner: We have no logo file, only the mark our sign painter put on the brick, and everything we hand out has to carry that same mark at every size on our dark ground without a white box around it.
client_brief:
Anvil and Oak, opening in March

We are two coaches opening a strength studio in a converted machine shop. Before this we ran a barbell club out of a shared space for six years, and about half our members are coming with us.

We have no logo file. What we have is the mark our sign painter put on the brick wall of the new space, and a photograph of it. Everything we hand out has to carry that mark, the same mark, at every size, and it has to sit on our dark ground.

We need the wall poster first. It hangs by the door and it is the weekly class grid: eight classes across five days, with times, coach and level. That grid changes with the season so we have to be able to change it ourselves.

We need the membership deck, the one we walk a prospect through at the desk. Our philosophy, how the programming actually works, who the coaches are, what the tiers cost and how to join. The tiers need to sit side by side so somebody can compare them in about four seconds.

We need the athlete cards. We ran these at the barbell club after every meet, one per lifter, their numbers and a line from them, and people kept them on their fridges. Our printer set those up and we only have the file that went to press. We want the same run for our opening roster, a proof of each, and a separate file per athlete.

And we need the spotlight posts: square for the feed, tall for stories, and the four by five one, all from the same portraits.

We shot the portraits ourselves over three evenings in the old space. They are not consistent and we know it.

We have nothing usable of the street or the building from outside. If there is something honest for the deck opener, use it.

Memberships run a hundred and ten to a hundred and eighty five a month, drop in twenty eight. Our people are twenty five to forty five and they are here to get strong. Confident, not soft, and not a bargain gym.
price_band_and_audience: Memberships at a hundred and ten to a hundred and eighty five dollars a month with a twenty eight dollar drop in, sold to twenty five to forty five year olds who are choosing coached strength work over a commodity gym and who read programming detail as evidence of competence. The band is load-bearing in both directions. At this price the correct grammar is confident and specific: a dark ground, cinematic portraits with real modelling on the shoulders and forearms, a schedule grid that shows level and coach rather than mood words, tier cards that state exactly what is included, and heavy condensed display type held in check by a plain workhorse text face. Softened into the pale, airy, thin-serif register of a boutique wellness studio it misreads the audience completely and reads as a place where nobody lifts anything heavy. Pushed the other way into shouted percentages, burst callouts and a discount-first hierarchy it becomes a chain gym promotion, which directly undercuts a price roughly double what the chains charge and tells a prospective member the coaching is not what they are paying for. A real posted commission of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: An independent strength and functional training studio selling coached memberships and drop in sessions.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opening March 2027 in a converted machine shop in Providence, Rhode Island, run by two coaches who ran a barbell club in a shared space for six years.
brand_identity.about: Anvil and Oak is a coach led strength studio built in an old machine shop. About half its opening members are following the two coaches from the barbell club they ran before. The offer is real programming and real coaching, not a commodity gym floor, and members read the detail of the programming as evidence the coaching is worth the price.
brand_identity.audience: People aged 25 to 45 choosing coached strength work over a commodity gym, here to get strong, who value programming detail and competence over amenities.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Memberships run 110 to 185 dollars a month with a 28 dollar drop in. Roughly double a chain gym, priced on coaching. Confident and specific, neither a soft boutique wellness studio nor a discount chain.
brand_identity.typography: Heavy condensed display type for headlines and the schedule grid, held in check by a plain workhorse sans for body, times and figures. Legible from across a room, comfortable at small sizes. Confident, unsoftened, industrial without being a novelty.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, plain and sure of itself, the way a good coach cues a lift. No hype, no percentages shouted. Example line the brand would write: Show up, do the work, add weight. We handle the programming so you can focus on the bar.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no logo file. The mark, an anvil silhouette inside a ring of lettering with an oak sprig crossing the anvil's horn, exists only as the sign painter's hand painted work on the studio's brick wall, which the coaches have photographed. Athlete portraits were shot by the coaches over three evenings and are not consistent. The old printer's press file is all that survives of the athlete card.
brand_identity.values: One mark, everywhere, complete and on the dark ground. The identity is the recovered wall mark used consistently, and the studio should always read as coached strength at its true price.

assets_supplied.name: wall_mark.jpg (approx 4000 x 3000)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the hand-painted studio mark on the raw brick wall of the new space, shot slightly off square in evening light: an anvil silhouette, a ring of lettering around it, and an oak sprig crossing the anvil's horn.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The mark our sign painter put on the brick. It is all we have."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup, and a selection aimed at it comes back plausible while quietly dropping one of its three elements, most often the sprig, which is thin and crosses the anvil. The enclosed counters inside the ring lettering are interior holes rather than outside edges, so a background removal returns an opaque patch of brick where the counters should be see-through.

assets_supplied.name: athlete_portraits/ (16 frames, three evenings, mixed dimensions)
assets_supplied.kind: Portraits of the opening roster shot by the coaches themselves over three evenings in the old shared space, on a mix of a camera and a phone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "We shot these ourselves over three evenings. They are not consistent and we know it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The three evenings sit at three different colour temperatures and two of them carry a green cast off the shared space's overhead tubes. Five frames are near-square captures that cannot reach the tall story format at native scale, and on two frames a loaded barbell crosses the subject at shoulder height so a subject selection takes it in on one frame and cuts through it on the other.

assets_supplied.name: meetcard_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The barbell club's flat press PDF for the post-meet athlete card, 5 by 7 inches portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the lifter's name, three stat lines, a quote line, the club crest and a tinted panel where the printed card shows the lifter's photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer set up. We only have what went to press and he is not doing this any more."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The crest and the panel behind the printed photograph were both drawn as artwork in the original layout rather than placed as images, so what the conversion exposes as addressable structure bears no relation to how the printed card is visually blocked out. Which of the printed lines are separately addressable and which share a single continuous flow cannot be inferred from looking at the card.

assets_supplied.name: roster_and_numbers.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The opening roster export from the club's spreadsheet, one row per athlete, with columns for name, three lift figures, level, coach and a quote line.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. One athlete asked to be left out after the export was taken and the request sits in the coaches' notes file rather than in the spreadsheet. The lift figures are a mix of kilograms and pounds with no unit column, so two athletes appear to be far stronger than they are. And two quote lines run to several times the length of the rest.

assets_supplied.name: coach_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A page from the two coaches on how the programming actually works, what each class level means, and a few lines about the roster.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How the programming works and what the levels mean."

acceptance_bar: One mark, not several. The mark on the poster, on the deck, on the cards and on every spotlight canvas is the same artwork placed identically, and it carries all three of its elements everywhere it appears.
The mark sits on the dark ground with no box, no halo and no white plate behind it, and it holds at the smallest size it is used at as well as the largest.

The sixteen portraits read as one shoot: one colour temperature, one black point, one degree of modelling on skin, one crop logic. An athlete who cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped near it.
Any invented edge added to reach a format is indistinguishable from the frame it extends when the finished canvas is viewed at full size on the dark ground.
No delivered image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop or resize operation's tradeoff record carries an enlargement entry.
Exactly one athlete card per rostered athlete who is in, no extra card and no missing card, and if the number shipped is not the roster count the note says which row was left out and why.
Every card's figures are true and comparable to every other card's figures, on a stated basis.

If a card cannot carry that athlete's photograph, the note says why in plain terms and the portrait is delivered somewhere the studio can actually use it, rather than the photograph being dropped in silence.
Each per-athlete file contains the athlete its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order files came back in.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The poster, the deck, the tier card and the spotlight set come back as one native editable document we can change times, prices and faces in, with every photograph actually visible, the schedule grid and the tier comparison as real tables, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.
The schedule grid reads at the distance a wall poster is read from, and the tier comparison can be understood in about four seconds.
The set reads as a coached strength studio at a hundred and ten to a hundred and eighty five a month, neither a soft wellness studio nor a discount chain.

A written note: what was applied to each portrait and why it differs, how the mark was recovered and at what size it stops holding, the type system by role, every roster row questioned and its resolution, what the press file conversion actually exposed, and every enlargement any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including trace and edge extension
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (global and masked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_vectorize, image_generative_expand, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs and detection_confidence)
adobe_surfaces.role: Two jobs on one surface. It recovers the mark off the photographed brick, which means selecting ink rather than substrate on a compound lockup, getting polarity right before tracing, and then repairing what the tracer hands back, since the trace arrives with no scalable frame and an opaque plate underneath it. And it brings sixteen portraits shot across three evenings to one look, then derives the platform formats, extending a frame's edge only where the tall format cannot be reached any other way. There is no measurement anywhere in this family and selections come back fully binary.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: The athlete card run, the only genuine record-per-page job in the engagement. The barbell club's press file becomes a live merge template, the roster becomes the data source after reconciliation, and the run yields the cards, the per-athlete single files the studio hands out, and the proofs the coaches approve. What that document actually exposes as addressable structure has to be read out of the exported interchange file rather than inferred from the printed card, the true story text reconstructed from its content runs, and the placeholder inventory confirmed by round trip rather than by a success message.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The A2 schedule poster at true physical dimensions, the five-root membership deck, the tier comparison card and the mixed-canvas spotlight set, all as one native editable document so the coaches can change times, prices and faces themselves. The recovered mark is inlined as vector markup so it stays editable rather than becoming a picture, every photograph is inlined as image data, the schedule grid and the tier comparison are genuine tables, family and weight are declared per text element, and each root declares its own canvas so the square, tall and four by five spotlight canvases coexist with an A2 sheet in one export.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the poster, the deck, the tier card and the spotlight set, and the only place the agent's typographic authorship exists, since no font chosen here can reach the printed athlete card. The pairing is the agent's own art direction against a confident, unsoftened strength band read from across a room, the numeric weight is non-standard per family so a heavy display cut cannot be reached by assuming a weight, one unlaundered name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the honest deck opener the studio does not own, IP-clean and at camera scale, with generative-tech candidates excluded, since the building's exterior does not exist as a usable photograph. The Boards half persists the portrait selects for the coaches' sign off, which matters here because the roster carries a consent question, placed within the twelve-per-call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: athlete cards to the merge surface, poster and deck and tier card and spotlight set to authored canvases, mark recovery and portraits to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The card is record per page against a layout the coaches want kept; everything else is free-form, seasonal and must stay editable, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the wall photograph, the sixteen portraits, the press PDF, the roster and the coaches' notes, holding each returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by athlete and by role, because the same portrait will exist in four states and the mark in at least three.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by athlete and role.

trajectory.action: Preview the wall photograph and decide how to name the mark so a selection lands on the painted ink rather than on the brick or the wall panel it sits in.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate and naming the graphic's own colour, medium and form pulls it to the ink. The lockup has three separable elements and one selection may not carry all of them.
trajectory.produces: A selection strategy and the mask or masks it produced, with a note on which elements each carried.

trajectory.action: Level the wall photograph, isolate the mark, get the polarity right, crop to its own bounds and trace it.
trajectory.judgement: Tracing the wrong polarity returns a filled plate with the mark knocked out of it, and both outcomes report success. What comes back from the tracer has no scalable frame and carries a full-canvas plate underneath the artwork, neither of which any tool repairs.
trajectory.produces: A traced mark with its frame injected and its underlying plate removed, ready to place on a dark ground.

trajectory.action: Place the recovered mark on the studio's dark ground at the sizes it will actually be used at, from the poster's header down to the corner of a story canvas and the athlete card's footer, and look at each one.
trajectory.judgement: A trace that reads correctly at the size it was traced is not evidence about the size it will be reproduced at, and the ground it sits on changes what survives. This is judged by looking, not by any readout.
trajectory.produces: The mark shown at every reproduction size it will be used at, on the real ground.

trajectory.action: Preview all sixteen portraits and triage: colour temperature per evening, cast, subject separation, what crosses the subject, native dimensions and how much edge each frame has to spare against each spotlight format.
trajectory.judgement: Three evenings are three different problems, and which frames can reach the tall format at native scale is a fact about the files rather than a decision.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note: session, cast, obstruction, native dimensions and edge margin per format.

trajectory.action: Fix one studio look and bring each of the sixteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Three colour temperatures and two casts have to arrive at one temperature and one black point, which is sixteen routes to one destination rather than one batched move, and the dark ground the portraits will sit on is what the black point has to answer to.
trajectory.produces: Sixteen graded portraits at source scale with a per-athlete parameter log.

trajectory.action: Lay the sixteen graded portraits together as the spotlight set will run them and judge them as one shoot.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set at the only moment the comparison exists, and deciding whether any portrait has been pushed far enough to stop belonging to the other fifteen.
trajectory.produces: A set judged as a set, with any portrait that will not join it named.

trajectory.action: Derive the square, four by five and tall spotlight crops from the graded masters, reading detection confidence and the tradeoff record on every crop, and extend the frame only where the tall format cannot otherwise be reached.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across sixteen athletes rather than sixteen good crops. Extending a frame is the only sanctioned way to add pixels and it is a last resort, not a default, and the tradeoffs array is the only place an enlargement toward the interpolation cap is ever reported.
trajectory.produces: Three families of spotlight crop with their tradeoff records, and a list of which frames were extended.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster against the coaches' notes, resolve the units question, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file and upload it.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation: one athlete's withdrawal lives in the notes and not in the spreadsheet, the lift figures are two different units presented as one column, and two quotes are far longer than the rest. Which of these is the agent's call and which is the coaches' is a decision, and the client asked to be told.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, a stated basis for the figures, and a list of roster questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF, export the interchange file, unzip it and read the real frame inventory and bounds, then reconstruct each frame's true story text from its concatenated content runs.
trajectory.judgement: What the document exposes is a property of how the club's printer built it, and every offset must be computed from the document's own text rather than from any convenience readout.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping against the structure the document actually exposes, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence, and ordering any rows that share a frame so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: A prepared template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document, render the athlete cards and the proofs at true print resolution from that document, and produce the per-athlete single files, naming each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per-record branch open, and identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that puts one lifter's numbers under another lifter's name.
trajectory.produces: The card run, print-resolution proofs, and per-athlete files verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card against the reconciled roster at trim rather than at proof scale, line by line and figure by figure.
trajectory.judgement: A card carrying another athlete's numbers and a card whose quote stops early both look like success at the API boundary and both look fine on a screen-scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A card-by-card reconciliation against the roster.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the honest deck opener, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the studio look and lay it against the graded portraits.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose blacks can live beside sixteen portraits already sitting on a dark ground rather than the moodiest thumbnail, and decide whether it joins the set or gets abandoned for a different search. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale opener, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to answer to a confident strength band read from across a room and to a schedule grid that must stay legible at small sizes. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML carrying the A2 poster at true physical dimensions, the five deck roots, the tier comparison card and the three spotlight canvases, inline the recovered mark as vector markup and every photograph as image data, set the schedule grid and the tier comparison as real tables, declare family and weight per text element, then upload it and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, vector markup in an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper runs off the canvas edge, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is a schedule grid that survives being read from six feet away and a tier comparison a prospect resolves in four seconds.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the poster, deck, tier card and spotlight set, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify the first canvas from the document's rendition and every other canvas from the returned per-canvas markup, then build the selects board within the placement cap and write the note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, the rendition shows the first artboard only, and a partial board placement is reported as a success. The note has to carry the consent question, the units basis and the mark's smallest safe size.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, a markup audit for the rest, a persistent board and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still holds where it is actually reproduced. The tracer takes no options at all, so everything about how the mark comes out is decided by the raster that goes in, and what comes back reads correctly at the size it was traced. On a hand-painted mark the ring lettering's counters and the gap between the oak sprig and the anvil's horn are narrow and irregular, and at the size the mark sits in a story canvas corner or a card footer, on the studio's dark ground rather than the pale field it was traced against, those counters can close up and the sprig can weld itself to the anvil. Nothing reports this. The artwork is valid, it places, it scales, and the failure exists only in what a person sees at reproduction size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot avoid it, because the mark must exist before it can be placed, and care cannot settle it, because the tracer exposes no threshold, no path simplification and no colour count, so there is no parameter to get right in advance. Nothing in the brief, the assets or the deliverables states that the mark has narrow counters or a tight gap; the client only states that the mark must hold at every size, which is their requirement rather than a disclosure. The response is not a re-run of the trace, it is a return to the raster preparation with a different bound and a different polarity, or an authored small-size variant of the mark, which is a design decision about what the mark is allowed to lose.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Go back into the raster preparation and re-isolate the mark on a bound that keeps the counters open, re-trace and re-repair the artwork, and if the counters still close at the smallest reproduction, author a deliberate small-size variant, then re-place both at every size on the dark ground and record which size the full lockup stops holding at so the studio knows where the line is.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A studio whose entire identity is one mark launches with that mark reading as a solid blob in the corner of every story post and at the foot of every athlete card, which is the one thing the client explicitly asked to be protected against and the thing every member will see most often.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether an extended frame can join the set. Five portraits are near-square captures that cannot reach the tall story format at native scale, so the only sanctioned route is to extend the frame's edges and crop into the result. What that extension actually builds is not knowable before it runs: it invents continuation from what is at the edge, and on a portrait shot in a cluttered shared space the invented edge can be a plausible wall that is nonetheless a different value and a different temperature from the graded set, or it can carry a smear where a rack upright ran off the frame. The call succeeds, returns a seed, and produces an image that looks entirely reasonable in isolation, on its own, at preview scale.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the frames that need extending are exactly the frames that cannot reach the format any other way, and enlargement is barred. Care cannot settle it either: nothing about a frame predicts what its edges will generate, and the same call on two portraits from the same evening can behave differently. Nothing in the brief or the assets says which frames are short or what sits at their edges, and the acceptance line about invented edges is the client's standing quality bar. The response is a composition decision rather than a re-run: extend from a different side, crop tighter and lose some of the athlete, or take that athlete out of the tall format and give them the square and four by five only.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay each extended frame against the graded set on the dark ground at full size rather than judging it alone at preview scale, and where the invented edge does not match, re-extend from a different side or accept a tighter crop, re-derive that athlete's spotlight canvases from the corrected master, and if no route works, drop that athlete from the tall format and say so rather than shipping a frame with an invented wall in it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The studio's launch story posts go out with five athletes standing in front of a wall that does not exist, in a value and a temperature that visibly disagree with the eleven portraits beside them, which reads to a prospective member as a cheaply faked photograph and undercuts a price roughly double what a chain gym charges.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the club's card actually exposes as addressable structure. The printed card reads as four separate blocks plus a crest and a photograph, but the crest and the panel behind the photograph were drawn as artwork rather than placed as images, and the printer's text blocks may or may not have been built as separate frames. Which lines are separately addressable, which share one continuous flow, and whether any graphic frame exists at all that a per-athlete portrait could be bound to, is a property of a document nobody involved has ever opened. The conversion reports success either way and the mapping readout will happily describe a structure that is nothing like the printed page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot avoid it, because the document has to be converted before it can be inspected, and no amount of study of the printed card predicts its internal construction. Nothing in the brief, the assets or the deliverables states how the printer built it; the client only says the printer set it up and is gone. It is not a propagation re-run, because if there is no graphic frame the portraits cannot be bound into the card at all, and the response is a re-plan of what the card is: a text-only merge run with the portraits carried into the spotlight set instead, put to the coaches as a change to what they asked for rather than decided silently.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the exported interchange file's real frame inventory before authoring any mapping, build the mapping against the structure that is actually there rather than the structure the printed card suggests, and if no frame can carry a per-athlete photograph, re-plan the card as a text run, deliver the portraits in a form the studio can use, and tell the coaches plainly why the card cannot hold the picture the old one appeared to hold.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The studio ships an opening-roster card run built on an imagined structure: fields mapped into frames that do not hold them, a portrait bound to nothing, and cards that come back looking like the old club card with lines missing or in the wrong place, discovered only when the coaches hand them to the members they were made for.

deliverables.name: Anvil and Oak mark, recovered as placeable scalable artwork
deliverables.spec: The studio mark recovered from a photograph of painted brick as artwork that scales, carries no plate behind it, and holds all three of its elements, delivered with whatever small-size variant the reproduction sizes turn out to require and a stated smallest safe size. It is placed identically on the poster, the deck, the tier card, the spotlight canvases and the athlete card, so the deliverable is one mark used consistently rather than several drawings of the same thing.

deliverables.name: Member-athlete portrait set, sixteen frames to one studio look plus the spotlight formats
deliverables.spec: Sixteen portraits shot across three evenings at three colour temperatures brought to one temperature, one black point and one degree of modelling, judged against the dark ground they will sit on, then derived into the square, four by five and tall formats under one crop logic. Polarity before tracing, where both the correct and the inverted result return success and only one is the mark.
What to do with a trace that arrives with no scalable frame and an opaque plate under it, neither of which any tool repairs.

One studio look across three evenings and two casts, and how far a portrait can be pushed toward it before it stops belonging to the set.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome dark gym poster with a redrawn anvil on it. IDENTITY: the mark is a specific hand-painted sign on this studio's own wall and the whole brief is that it must be recovered rather than reinterpreted, and the athletes are named members whose faces and numbers appear on cards they will keep. SPEC: the run is one 5 by 7 card per rostered athlete binding named fields verbatim on one stated basis, plus per-athlete single files each containing the athlete they claim and proofs at true print resolution, alongside three named social formats derived without adding pixels. EDITABILITY: the poster, the deck and the tier card are defined by being editable, because the schedule changes with the season and the prices change with it. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this trace still hold at card-footer size on the dark ground, does this extended edge match the set, does this document expose anything that can carry a photograph.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments global and masked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, vectorize, generative_expand and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence are all verified headless, and the extract-and-reuse chain from a photographed printed mark through to native editable vector inside an exported document is verified end to end. The mark checkpoint rests on documented facts rather than invention: vectorize takes no options at all so all tuning must happen in the raster prep, its output has no viewBox and always carries a full-canvas background rectangle as path zero, selection on a compound mark is documented as silently dropping elements, and remove_background is documented as unable to punch an enclosed interior hole. The extension checkpoint rests on generative_expand being the single sanctioned generative call, documented as adding pixels only at the edges with content that is AI generated, while crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating up to a hard 2x cap reported only in the tradeoffs array, which is what makes the no-enlargement bar checkable rather than asserted. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool, the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored so proofs must be rendered from the merged document, multi-record raster URL order is documented as unreliable so identity must be established by opening files, frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not under the agent's control with a verified case collapsing to one text frame and zero graphic frames, and the mapping readout's textContent is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases at 96 dpi, real tables with per-cell strokes, inline SVG as native editable vector, and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows page one only so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; the payload is routed by uploaded URL because inlined portraits pass the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve-per-call board cap with a partial success read as partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no variable QR, no bleed or press-preset gate, no batch above 20.
